chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Honi Coles credits him with starting the rhythm; new steps
summary: Nierenberg recalls Coles saying from the stage that Bubbles started the rhythm tap; Bubbles says dancers watched four rows deep to catch his steps.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Before we get into this. I know last Friday night at the performance at Royce Hall, Tap Two, Honey Coles said from the stage, pointing to you, "There's the man that's responsible for rhythm. The rhythm that you saw us doing on the stage -- there's the man that really started it."
Well there must have been a lot of people that were watching you, lot of other dancers that were seeing what you were doing, you must have been
feeling -- there must have been a progression that you were going through as a tap dancer at this time as well, wasn't there?
Weren't you exploring more into the medium and creating new types of steps that they had never seen before?

Yeah, I was doing that, yeah. Yeah, I was working more than any other actor so they get to see me more. People used to come and watch us sometimes, four deep -- four rows deep in the theater watching our show, trying to catch steps I was doing.
Well, what was it that you were doing in your dancing that was so new?

Doing what I was doing -- the steps I was doing I was doing in different ways. I did new steps and I did old steps and turned them into something else. That's the way I tap danced, that's the way it was. It's hard to explain it. Very hard to explain it.
